**Additional data point: faulting IP disassembles to a deliberate `ud2` panic, not an AVX/illegal-SIMD instruction**

- opencode **1.17.11** (latest), bundled `Bun v1.3.14 (Linux x64 baseline)`
- WSL2 kernel `6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, Intel i7-12700K (avx2, **no avx512**), 41 GiB RAM (not OOM; 19 GiB free, load 1.68 at crash)
- dmesg:
  ```
  traps: HeapHelper[...] trap invalid opcode ip:2607064 ... in opencode[24c8000+36e6000]
  opencode: HeapHelper: potentially unexpected fatal signal 4
  ```

The binary is `ET_EXEC`, so the runtime IP maps 1:1 to the file. `objdump -d` at `0x2607064`:

```
2607045: e8 36 de 02 00   call 2634e80      # memset-loop helper (calls memset@plt)
260705f: e8 1c de 02 00   call 2634e80
2607064: 0f 0b            ud2               # <-- faulting IP
2607066: cc               int3              # int3 padding (noreturn site)
...
2607070: 55               push %rbp         # clean next-function prologue
```

This is a **deliberate panic/abort trap** (`ud2`) on the Bun/JSC GC thread (`HeapHelper`), reached just after a memset/allocation helper — **not** a CPU-incompatible SIMD instruction. The binary embeds Rust panic machinery (`std::panicking::begin_panic_handler`, `std::panicking::rust_panic_with_hook`); `ud2` is the standard Rust/Zig panic→abort trap.

**Triage note for the broader "invalid opcode" bucket (incl. #33595):** a Bun/Zig `ud2` panic produces the **identical** kernel `trap invalid opcode` / `fatal signal 4` message as a genuine missing-AVX illegal instruction. The two are only distinguishable by disassembling the faulting IP. This instance is unambiguously a **GC/runtime panic** (this issue / #22084 bucket), not an AVX-baseline mismatch — the CPU here has no AVX-512 yet the binary is the `baseline` build, and the trapping byte is `0f 0b ud2`, not an EVEX/zmm op.

Reproduced on the latest **1.17.11**, so the current release does not fix it. Crash recovered cleanly via process auto-restart; application state intact. Aggravating context: high concurrency (3+ primary sessions in one project + several vite dev servers) → elevated GC pressure on the `HeapHelper` thread.

Cross-ref / disambiguation from #33890: I hit the same `trap invalid opcode` / `fatal signal 4` kernel signature (opencode 1.17.11, bundled `Bun v1.3.14 Linux x64 baseline`, WSL2, Intel i7-12700K with avx2 but no avx512), but disassembling the exact faulting IP shows the trapping byte is `0f 0b` (**`ud2`**) — a deliberate Bun/JSC GC panic→abort on the `HeapHelper` thread, immediately followed by `int3` padding and a clean next-function prologue. Not an EVEX/zmm/AVX-512 instruction.

So at least some reports in this "baseline may not be truly baseline" bucket are actually **runtime panics** (the `ud2` path, see #33890 / #22084), which the kernel reports with the identical `trap invalid opcode` message as a genuine missing-CPU-feature illegal instruction. Suggest triagers `objdump` the faulting IP to split the two buckets: `0f 0b ud2` ⇒ runtime panic; an EVEX-encoded SIMD op ⇒ true baseline/AVX mismatch. Full disassembly evidence in #33890.

Reproducible on **1.17.11** (and 1.17.8), and this is a **real listener leak on client disconnect** — not a false/benign "normal fanout" warning (cf. #23798). It is the runtime side of the now-closed #15645 / #17628, which still reproduces.

### Minimal reproduction (no plugins)

```sh
cd <any git repo>
opencode web --pure --port 4199 --print-logs --log-level INFO &
sleep 3
# open + immediately drop the event stream 16x (what a browser does on refresh/navigate/reconnect):
for i in $(seq 1 16); do
  curl -s --max-time 1 -H "x-opencode-directory: $PWD" http://127.0.0.1:4199/event >/dev/null
done
```

Result: `MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventTarget memory leak detected. 11 event listeners added to [..]` (event name `"event"`, Effect `evaluate` stack) — identical to the report above. `--pure` (zero plugins) rules out any plugin cause.

### Root cause

The `--print-logs` output shows **16× `global event connected` and 0× `global event disconnected`**. The SSE finalizer in `eventResponse()` never runs on disconnect:

`packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/global.ts`
```ts
const events = Stream.callback<GlobalBusEvent>((queue) => {
  const handler = (event) => Queue.offerUnsafe(queue, event)
  return Effect.acquireRelease(
    Effect.sync(() => GlobalBus.on("event", handler)),
    () => Effect.sync(() => GlobalBus.off("event", handler)),  // never runs on abort
  )
})
// ...
Stream.ensuring(Effect.logInfo("global event disconnected")),   // never logs on abort
```

The stream scope isn't tied to the request's abort signal, so a TCP CLOSE-WAIT (client gone) never finalizes the scope → `GlobalBus.off(...)` and the 10s heartbeat cleanup never fire. **Each event-stream connection permanently leaks one `GlobalBus` `"event"` listener** (+ its heartbeat interval). Browsers reconnect the stream routinely, so the count crosses Node's default `defaultMaxListeners` (10) in normal use; long sessions grow unbounded (the 7GB / unresponsive behavior in #17628).

### Note

This is **not** fixed by bumping `setMaxListeners` — that hides a genuine unbounded leak. The fix is to interrupt the SSE stream scope when the request aborts so the existing `acquireRelease` / `Stream.ensuring` cleanup actually runs.

Cross-ref: this is the same `/event` SSE-disconnect listener leak now addressed by **#31922** (Closes #22198) — it bounds the per-subscriber SSE backlog and ends/unsubscribes consumers stuck in CLOSE_WAIT, touching exactly `server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/global.ts` + `event.ts`. The mechanism there matches the repro in my comment above (N× `global event connected`, 0× `global event disconnected`). Still reproduces on 1.17.11, so worth tracking/merging under #31922.

## Root cause: Ollama Cloud returns `prompt_tokens: 0` and no `reasoning_tokens` for `minimax-m3:cloud`

Reproduced on **opencode 1.17.8 + Ollama 0.30.11** with the same model family the original reporter used. Have diagnostic data — figured I'd share.

### Direct API probe (curl against `https://ollama.com/v1/chat/completions`)

**`minimax-m3:cloud` — request that should produce ~15-25 prompt tokens:**

```bash
curl -X POST https://ollama.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"minimax-m3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a 200-word essay about why path tracers are elegant."}],"max_tokens":400,"stream":false}'
```

Response `usage` block:
```json
"usage": { "prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 400, "total_tokens": 400 }
```

**`prompt_tokens: 0`** for a non-trivial prompt. Verified across three different request sizes — all returned `prompt_tokens: 0`. The `total_tokens` is just the `max_tokens` ceiling (400), not actual output.

### Control: same endpoint, sibling model `minimax-m2.1`

Same "Hi" greeting request:
```json
"usage": { "prompt_tokens": 39, "completion_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 49 }
```

`m2.1` reports input correctly. The issue is specific to `minimax-m3:cloud`'s deployment on Ollama Cloud.

### Why the DUI counter jumps back to ~1k

Looking at `packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts` `getUsage`:
- Reads `usage.inputTokens` → `0` from the API
- Reads `usage.outputTokens` → reports up to `max_tokens` ceiling, not actual content length
- `output = outputTokens - reasoningTokens` → `reasoningTokens` is also `undefined`, falls back to `0`

So the per-turn counter is effectively showing output-only, and the "jumps back to 1k" is the displayed value resetting between turns because the model genuinely reports zero inputs each request. The reasoning field is *populated* in `choices[0].message.reasoning` — opencode reads from the wrong location (`usage.reasoning_tokens` doesn't exist on this endpoint).

### Two distinct telemetry bugs in the same deployment

| Field | What's broken | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `prompt_tokens` | Always 0 | Ollama Cloud wrapper for m3 |
| `reasoning_tokens` | Always 0 | Reasoning emitted in `message.reasoning`, opencode reads `usage.reasoning_tokens` |

### Impact

- Per-turn counter is meaningless for cost estimation or context window tracking on this model
- "Free tier" dream isn't real either — local Ollama app log shows intermittent `403 Forbidden: this model requires a subscription, upgrade for access` errors (ref `f52d9312-0f8d-46a2-9e29-fbcf4c495d6a`), so something on Ollama's side is gating access even though `~/.ollama/cache/model-recommendations.json` lists m3 as `required_plan: "free"`

### Suggested fix paths (for maintainers)

1. **Opencode fallback**: in `getUsage`, when `usage.inputTokens === 0` for an Ollama provider, estimate input from the request payload (use a local tokenizer like `gpt-tokenizer` on the messages array). This avoids depending on the upstream API reporting correctly.
2. **Reasoning fallback**: also read `choices[0].message.reasoning?.length` (or the model's actual reasoning token field) as a fallback for `reasoningTokens`.
3. **Ollama Cloud side**: file a parallel bug — the wrapper for `minimax-m3:cloud` is dropping `prompt_tokens` from the OpenAI-compatible response. Not opencode's bug to fix alone.

### Versions

- opencode: 1.17.8 (Choco install)
- Ollama: 0.30.11 (Windows)
- Model: `minimax-m3:cloud` (also responds to bare `minimax-m3`)
- Provider config: `npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"`, baseURL `https://ollama.com/v1`

A bit more detail on the code path for the maintainers:

The crash originates in `packages/app/src/app.tsx` around lines 137-139 in `ResolvedTargetSessionRoute`:

```ts
sync.session.lineage.resolve(id).catch((error) => {
  if (isSessionNotFoundError(error, id)) tabs.removeSessionTab({ server, sessionId: id })
  throw error   // <-- re-throws, causing the resource to go into errored state
})
```

The handler correctly detects the `SessionNotFoundError` and removes the stale tab, but then **re-throws** the error. This causes the `resolved` resource to remain in an `"errored"` state, and the fallback `ErrorPage` is rendered instead of gracefully falling through.

Meanwhile, the tab removal propagates back to the persisted store (`default.dat` / `opencode.global.dat`), so the stale session ID is eventually cleaned up — but the user still sees an error page on the current view.

PR #32085 fixes a similar issue in `directory-sync.ts`, but this `app.tsx` path also needs the same treatment: after `removeSessionTab`, the error should not be re-thrown, or the route should redirect to a safe default (e.g., new session or project view).
I frequently see the TUI running in Warp using 100% cpu usage sitting idle during a long session using GPT 5.5.

Another data point: the same stale session problem also applies to the `"tabs"` array in `opencode.global.dat`. On my machine, all 3 persisted session tabs were stale. After removing the first stale tab and restarting, closing the remaining tab caused a cascade - the app tried to switch to the next stale tab in the list and crashed again with the same `Session not found` error. Only after clearing all stale entries from `"tabs"` did the app behave normally.

So the persisted session tab list is another vector for this bug, not just `lastProjectSession`. A fix should handle stale session IDs anywhere they're stored: `lastProjectSession`, `"tabs"`, and possibly `sessionTabs` in the layout state.
